blockers.quote: The most common regret of a life is education: about a third of all regrets (c11).
blockers.why: Overstated scope. The source (Roese & Summerville 2005 meta-analysis of 11 regret ranking studies) found education accounted for 32.2% of regrets across those specific studies, but the draft states this as an unqualified universal truth about human life ('of a life'). C11 in claims.md explicitly scopes the claim to 'Across eleven studies'.
blockers.fix: Across eleven studies, the most common life regret was education: about a third of all regrets (c11).

blockers.quote: Here's what you had backwards. The curve was never your class. In most subjects, it's the top 4 per cent of everyone in the country who sat it (c01). His grade never cost you yours.
blockers.why: The wrong belief is framed as a straw man (rules/story.md #7). No high school senior preparing for Korea's national entrance exam genuinely believes the national percentile curve is computed only across their own 100-student classroom. Dropping c13 (the school-level internal naesin curve) turned what was a genuine structural conflict into an implausible misunderstanding. The misconception should be framed as treating a percentage threshold as a fixed local quota of seats.
blockers.fix: You treated the four per cent like four seats in a room. But in most subjects, it's the top 4 per cent of everyone in the country who sat it (c01). His grade never cost you yours.
